candidate.title: PAT-ChIP
candidate.scope: The single linear PAT-ChIP (pathology tissue chromatin immunoprecipitation) schematic for FFPE-derived chromatin, ending at purified immunoprecipitated DNA. The left title vignette is descriptive and has no transfer arrow into the workflow; fixation and paraffin embedding are input history. The verified collection-page heading and caption identify PAT-ChIP alone. FiT-seq is mentioned and cited as a refinement in surrounding catalogue text but is neither a depicted alternative nor a grouped target here. The architecture describes the material that can feed ChIP-seq; downstream library construction and sequencing are outside the drawn route.

operations.label: Deparaffination and rehydration
operations.description: Remove the embedding paraffin from FFPE pathology material and rehydrate it, making FFPE-derived chromatin available for the following digestion.
operations.mechanism: The catalogue specifies dewaxing with the xylene substitute Histolemon; it supplies the method-distinguishing reagent identity without requiring an unshown solvent-exchange recipe.
operations.information_effect: Changes the tissue preparation state before chromatin fragmentation; it does not perform target-specific selection.

operations.label: MNase digestion
operations.description: Digest the rehydrated FFPE-derived chromatin with MNase, producing nuclease-fragmented chromatin represented by the shorter nucleosome array before sonication.
operations.mechanism: Nuclease digestion of chromatin-associated DNA, as named by the caption. Orange circles occur at this stage, but no legend assigns them a chemical identity or a measured histone mark.
operations.information_effect: Changes the physical fragmentation of chromatin while leaving protein-associated DNA available for the subsequent affinity selection.

operations.label: Sonicate
operations.description: Sonicate the MNase-digested chromatin to yield the depicted soluble extract for immunoprecipitation.
operations.mechanism: Physical disruption by sonication, following nuclease digestion in the drawn route; no separate clarification operation or precise fragment distribution is specified.
operations.information_effect: Makes chromatin available as a soluble DNA-protein substrate. The catalogue warns that sonication may introduce sequence bias; the cited study documents chromatin-dependent shearing and recovery effects in yeast, rather than quantifying PAT-ChIP-specific bias.

method_scopes.rationale: All six local operations form the single captioned PAT-ChIP route: deparaffination/rehydration, MNase digestion, sonication to soluble extract, immunoprecipitation/elution, crosslink reversal/proteinase K digestion and purification to DNA. Soluble extract and DNA are material labels, not extra operations. The yellow-DNA title vignette, orange circles at MNase digestion, affinity glyph and enzyme-like proteinase icon do not establish extra branches, target identities or terminal chemistry. Fanelli et al. is associated with PAT-ChIP by the literal card reference and its own abstract; its abstract supports assay identity, FFPE input and possible readouts, while the diagram establishes the local operation order. Full protocol text is not supplied. No step is assigned to FiT-seq merely from the shared catalogue description.

checks.rationale: Independent inspection supports the complete candidate at its declared schematic scope: one PAT-ChIP route, seven material states, six local transformations and twelve material edges. The final DNA carries genomic association with the enrichment target into possible downstream ChIP-seq; library construction is outside the displayed route. The candidate distinguishes catalogue evidence, abstract-level PAT-ChIP support and the available background full text. There is no consequential source conflict requiring a correction, no unsupported method expansion and no blocking architecture unknown.
